body.message:
Thank you for your response.

We do not agree with the deduction of AED 1,400, and your explanation does not withstand factual and procedural review.

1. No issue was identified at check-out  
Your own inspection conducted at the time of our check-out did not identify any bed bug issue, nor was any such matter raised, documented, or signed by us at that time.

2. Post check-out claims are not valid  
The alleged “bed bug issue” was introduced only after check-out, which makes it a post-factum claim. Any such claim cannot be attributed to the tenant without clear, contemporaneous, and signed evidence.

3. Your own documentation contradicts your claim  
The pest control service report provided does not establish tenant responsibility and does not confirm that the issue originated during our stay or was caused by us.

4. No signed agreement to any deduction  
At no point did we agree to any deduction of AED 1,400. There is no signed document, inspection report, or acknowledgment from our side supporting this deduction.

5. Lack of causal link  
Even if treatment was carried out, you have not demonstrated any causal link between the alleged issue and our stay, which is required to justify any deduction from the security deposit.

Based on the above, the deduction is unjustified and not enforceable.

We will be updating the DET complaint accordingly to reflect:
– partial payment only
– unjustified withholding of AED 1,400
– unsupported post check-out claims

We request once again that the remaining AED 1,400 be transferred immediately to fully settle this matter.

Kindly confirm once completed.
